name: model-preferences-routing
title: Model Preferences
purpose: TUI for managing per-agent/per-command model preferences in OpenCode. Users pick a model for each agent or command, then apply to write preferences to opencode.json.

requirements.title: Preferences Config in Separate File
requirements.body: Preferences (target-to-model mappings) must be stored in a separate file (~/.config/opencode/omp-preferences.json), NOT in opencode.json. This is required because opencode.json uses additionalProperties:false and rejects unknown keys. The path must respect OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR.

scenarios.title: Preferences path respects OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR
given: OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR is set to a custom directory
then: returns {OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR}/omp-preferences.json

scenarios.title: Missing file returns empty config
given: omp-preferences.json does not exist
then: returns empty PreferencesConfig with no error

scenarios.title: Writes are atomic
given: a preferences config to save
then: writes to a temp file then renames
no temp files remain after success

requirements.title: Apply Preferences
requirements.body: Applying preferences writes the assigned model to each target's model field in opencode.json. Uses sjson for surgical JSON path updates that preserve formatting. Only writes to targets that already exist in opencode.json (does not create new entries). Targets without an assignment are left unchanged.

scenarios.title: Model applied to agent
given: a preference mapping build to 'anthropic/claude-opus-4'
agent build exists in config
then: agent.build.model is set to 'anthropic/claude-opus-4'

scenarios.title: Model applied to command
given: a preference mapping deploy to 'anthropic/claude-opus-4'
command deploy exists in config
then: command.deploy.model is set to 'anthropic/claude-opus-4'

scenarios.title: Only writes to existing config entries
given: a target exists in discovery but has no entry in opencode.json
then: no new agent/command entry is created in opencode.json

scenarios.title: No assignment leaves target unchanged
given: a target has no entry in preferences
then: the target's model in opencode.json is not modified

scenarios.title: Empty model leaves target unchanged
given: a target has an empty string model in preferences
then: the target's model in opencode.json is not modified

requirements.title: Dual-File Persistence
requirements.body: The system uses two config files: opencode.json for agent/command model assignments (written by ApplyPreferences), and omp-preferences.json for preference mappings (written by SavePreferences). Writes to opencode.json use tidwall/sjson for surgical JSON path updates that preserve formatting. Writes to omp-preferences.json use atomic temp+rename.

scenarios.title: sjson preserves formatting
given: opencode.json has existing formatting
then: existing structure is preserved
only model fields are updated

scenarios.title: Preferences config is separate from opencode.json
given: opencode.json uses additionalProperties:false
then: preferences are written to omp-preferences.json, not opencode.json

requirements.title: Model Discovery
requirements.body: Models are discovered using a CLI-first strategy: run 'opencode models' to get the live model list, falling back to parsing provider.*.models from opencode.json if the CLI fails or returns empty. On startup, 'opencode models --refresh' is called to update the provider registry.

scenarios.title: CLI models used when available
given: opencode models returns a list of models
then: CLI models are used, not config models

scenarios.title: Falls back to config when CLI fails
given: opencode models fails or returns empty
then: models are parsed from provider.*.models in opencode.json

scenarios.title: Refresh runs on startup
given: omp is launched
then: opencode models --refresh is called before loading config

requirements.title: Agent Filtering
requirements.body: System agents (compaction, title, summary) must be excluded from target discovery. All other agents (built-in user-facing and user-defined) must be included.

scenarios.title: System agents excluded
given: config has agents: build, plan, compaction, title, summary
then: build and plan are included
compaction, title, and summary are excluded

requirements.title: Target Discovery
requirements.body: The system discovers targets from three sources: built-in agents (build, plan as primary/locked; general, explore as subagent), markdown agent/command files (global + project directories), and JSON-configured agents/commands in opencode.json. Markdown mode wins over JSON default. Hidden agents are tracked but filtered in display.

scenarios.title: Built-in agents always present
given: an empty opencode.json
then: build, plan, general, explore are present

scenarios.title: Markdown mode wins over JSON default
given: a markdown agent with mode: subagent
a JSON entry for the same agent with no mode
then: the agent's mode is 'subagent' (from markdown, not 'all' from JSON default)

scenarios.title: Project agents discovered from .opencode directory
given: a .opencode/agents/ directory exists in the project tree
then: markdown agents from the project directory are included

requirements.title: Single-View TUI
requirements.body: The TUI displays a single list of agents and commands with their current model assignment. Users pick a model via a filterable picker, clear assignments, and apply all preferences to opencode.json.

scenarios.title: Agents and commands listed with sections
given: agents and commands exist
then: agents appear under an 'Agents' section header
commands appear under a 'Commands' section header

scenarios.title: Hidden agents excluded from display
given: an agent has hidden: true in frontmatter
then: the hidden agent does not appear in the list

scenarios.title: Model picker shows discovered models
given: models are discovered from CLI or config
scenarios.when: the user presses enter/m on a target
then: a filterable picker shows all discovered model IDs plus a clear option
